distractors: Demagnetization is required when a residual field would cause problems.
Routine equipment checks keep the system valid.
Electrical and UV hazards must be controlled, not ignored.

content.stem: A Level I MT operator under API 1104 mainly:
options: Signs off the final disposition of the weld
Magnetizes, applies particles, and records them
Writes the acceptance criteria for the method itself
Qualifies the welding procedure for the joint
distractors: Disposition is above Level I.
Criteria come from the standard.
WPS qualification is separate.
content.explanation: Level I performs the examination and records indications; evaluation sits above Level I.

content.stem: MT can be used on welds that are:
options: Ferromagnetic and able to hold a field
Non-ferromagnetic, such as aluminum alloys
Non-metallic and unable to be magnetized
Coated and painted on the test surface
distractors: Non-ferromagnetic parts use PT.
Non-metals cannot be magnetized.
Paint interferes with MT.
content.explanation: MT requires a ferromagnetic material to hold a magnetic field.

content.stem: MT reveals discontinuities that are:
options: Deep within the volume of the weld
At or just below the surface of the part
Only at mid-wall in the cross section itself
Only on the internal bore surface
distractors: MT does not find deep flaws.
Mid-wall is beyond MT.
Internal flaws are beyond MT.
content.explanation: MT finds surface and slightly subsurface discontinuities.

content.stem: A non-relevant MT indication arises from:
options: An actual crack opening at the surface
A rejectable defect found within the weld metal body
A through-wall hole opening right through the joint wall
Part geometry or a section change, not a discontinuity
distractors: A crack is relevant.
A defect is relevant.
A hole is a real feature.
content.explanation: Non-relevant indications come from part geometry, section or permeability changes, or magnetic writing, and are screened out before evaluation.

content.stem: The magnetic field for MT can be set up with a:
options: A radiation source aimed at the joint
A yoke or prods placed on the part
A penetrameter laid beside the weld
A film of couplant on the surface
distractors: MT is not radiographic.
Penetrameters are radiographic.
Couplant is for UT.
content.explanation: A yoke or prods establish the field that forms particle indications.

content.stem: Full MT coverage of a weld needs magnetization in:
options: Two roughly perpendicular field directions
One single direction across the weld
A single random pass over the surface itself
No set direction across the part
distractors: One direction misses parallel flaws.
One pass is insufficient.
Direction matters.
content.explanation: Two perpendicular directions catch discontinuities of any orientation.

content.stem: Adequate field strength is confirmed with a:
options: A density strip read against the film itself
A penetrameter set beside the weld
A couplant gauge held to the part
A field indicator or a qualified technique
distractors: Density strips are radiographic.
Penetrameters are radiographic.
Couplant gauges are for UT.
content.explanation: Field adequacy is verified with an indicator such as a pie gauge.

content.stem: Visible particle indications are read under:
options: Total darkness across the work area
Ultraviolet light only on the part
Adequate white light on the surface
No particular light level at all
distractors: Visible particles need light.
UV is for fluorescent particles.
Light level matters.
content.explanation: Visible particles are evaluated under adequate white light.

content.stem: A crack found by MT is:
options: Acceptable on the part whenever it is short
Acceptable as long as it sits off the root
Classed as a non-relevant indication
Rejectable wherever it appears on the weld
distractors: Length does not exempt it.
Location does not exempt it.
A crack is relevant.
content.explanation: Cracks are rejectable.

content.stem: Relevant indications found at Level I are:
options: Erased from the part to save effort
Reported only verbally to the next hand
Recorded for the later evaluation step
Left for the next crew to deal with
distractors: Data is retained.
Records are documented.
Recording is not deferred.
content.explanation: Relevant indications are documented for Level II/company evaluation.

content.stem: Acceptance criteria are applied by the:
options: The Level I operator running the test
The Level II evaluator or the company
The particle supplier providing the bath
The pipe mill that supplied the joint
distractors: Level I records, not dispositions.
Suppliers do not interpret.
The mill supplies pipe.
content.explanation: Evaluation against the criteria is a Level II/company function.

content.stem: Demagnetization after MT is done when residual fields could:
options: Improve the coating applied to the pipe
Add to the overall strength of the joint itself
Disturb later welding, machining, or service
Thin the measured wall of the pipe
distractors: It does not aid coating.
It does not add strength.
It does not change thickness.
content.explanation: Residual magnetism is removed where it could interfere with subsequent operations.

content.stem: An MT-rejected area after repair is:
options: Re-examined to the same method and criteria
Accepted on the strength of the repair note
Judged the second time by relaxed limits
Exempt from re-test once it is repaired
distractors: A note is not re-inspection.
Limits do not relax.
Re-examination is required.
content.explanation: The repair is re-inspected to the same basis.

content.stem: MT is preferred over PT when the part is:
options: Ferromagnetic and able to hold a field
Non-ferromagnetic, such as aluminum alloys
Non-metallic and unable to be magnetized
Coated on the outside of the pipe
distractors: Non-ferromagnetic parts use PT.
Non-metals cannot be magnetized.
Coating blocks both.
content.explanation: MT suits ferromagnetic parts; PT covers materials that cannot be magnetized.

content.stem: MT for API 1104 compliance is performed by personnel who are:
options: Members of the welding crew on the spread
Chosen by lottery among the available hands
Qualified and certified for the MT method
Approved by the coating crew on the line
distractors: Welders are not the NDT authority.
Qualification is not by chance.
Coaters do not certify MT.
content.explanation: Examinations are performed by qualified, certified MT personnel.
